headline: Gemini is coming to your Mac to do stuff for you
summary: Only one thing worth a look today: Gemini for Mac can now operate your computer for you.

items.title: Gemini for Mac can operate your computer directly
actions: In the Gemini Mac app, type @Computer use in the prompt, then write what you want done
Requirements: US region, English, a Google AI Plus/Pro/Ultra subscription, a personal account aged 18+, and an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 15 or later
deep_dive: Reportedly you can limit which apps it's allowed to use, stop it any time, and it needs your approval before doing anything sensitive.
It runs in an isolated background window, so you can keep using your computer. That's different from tools that take over your mouse directly.

For now it's US and English only, and Google hasn't said when it'll reach other regions. Macworld says the feature is "coming soon," while other outlets say it's already out, so the reports don't quite match.
items.signals: Josh Woodward's tweet: 876 likes · 35 retweets · just one tweet, so not much detail
items.what: Gemini's Mac app has a new "computer use" feature. When you write @Computer use in the prompt, Gemini clicks, scrolls and types for you in a separate background window, handling tasks in folders, apps and web pages. Your screen and mouse stay untouched, and you can watch live in the window what it's doing. The official demo turns a sketch into a 3D model in Blender.
items.meaning: Even people who can't code can get AI to operate their computer, and it goes head-to-head with similar features from Claude and Codex. You need a paid Google subscription to use it, so it probably doesn't affect you much.

items.title: ChatGPT mobile gets a big redesign
items.signals: Thibault Sottiaux's tweet: 5,244 likes · 276 retweets · another one mentions 1.2 billion users
items.what: OpenAI is testing a new look for the ChatGPT mobile app, aimed at making the features you use most easier to find. You can pin Codex (the AI that writes code), Projects (project folders), Images (image generation) and more to a tab bar at the bottom. A "dot" is an AI assistant in ChatGPT that keeps running in the background, and in the new design each dot gets its own tab.
items.meaning: It's just an interface tweak with no new abilities. It'll be handy if you want to open Codex quickly on your phone.
actions: In ChatGPT, go to Settings > New ChatGPT Design to switch the new look on or off any time
For now it's going to Pro users who have a dot or are eligible to create one, and some of them will see it by default
deep_dive: OpenAI also says it's testing dots with a small group of Plus users and rolling them out to all Business Standard users.
Per the official notes, creating a dot has to be done on desktop. Pro users in the European Economic Area, Switzerland and the UK won't have it at first.
OpenAI says it wants feedback before the full rollout, so the design may change again.

still_tracking.name: Gemini 4 Neon
still_tracking.update: After comparing it with Opus 5.5, Peter Yang says he'd use Neon for 99% of his tasks, and that its writing and personality are just as good. Simon Willison complained that the pricing is a mess, and Neon is the priciest right now.
